provenance.authoring_method: LLM-authored analytical examples with fixture-verified numeric examples

warning: Optional synthetic methods, never current facts or authorization. Adapt or ignore; query current scoped data.

examples.description: Count modeled unsold units at a business cutoff.
examples.example_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT inventory_id) AS units FROM stock
examples.illustrative_answer: At the demonstration cutoff, the authorized records contain 5 modeled unsold units. This is not a statement about physical availability or reservations.
method_notes: stock applies the trusted as_of; use inventory for a different explicit cutoff.
Keep physical snapshot_at separate from business as_of.

examples.example_sql: SELECT product_id, product_name, COUNT(DISTINCT inventory_id) AS units FROM stock GROUP BY product_id, product_name ORDER BY units DESC, product_id
examples.illustrative_answer: Demo Linen Shirt and Demo Wool Jacket each have 2 modeled unsold units; Demo Canvas Bag has 1. These counts alone do not identify excess stock or unmet demand.
method_notes: Count inventory IDs, not duplicated sales rows.

examples.example_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT inventory_id) AS aged_units FROM stock WHERE created_at <= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 90 DAY)
examples.illustrative_answer: Two modeled unsold units were created at least 90 days before the demonstration cutoff. Age identifies records to investigate; it does not establish damage or obsolescence.
method_notes: Define threshold inclusivity and age from created_at.
Do not treat missing timestamps as zero age.

examples.description: Report inventory cost with missing-value coverage.
examples.example_sql: SELECT SUM(cost) AS known_cost, COUNT(cost) AS costed_units, COUNT(*) AS units FROM stock
examples.illustrative_answer: Known recorded cost totals 97.50 across 4 of 5 modeled unsold units. One unit has no cost, so a complete valuation is unavailable; the source does not specify currency.
method_notes: Report SUM(cost) alongside non-null count and total.
Do not replace missing cost with zero or equate cost with profit.

examples.example_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT inventory_id) AS units FROM inventory WHERE created_at <= TIMESTAMP '2026-03-01 00:00:00+00' AND (sold_at IS NULL OR sold_at > TIMESTAMP '2026-03-01 00:00:00+00') AND (sold_at IS NULL OR sold_at >= created_at)
examples.illustrative_answer: The current demonstration records reconstruct 4 modeled unsold units as of March 1. This does not prove what the warehouse knew at that historical time.
method_notes: Apply both creation and sale cutoffs.
A sale exactly at the cutoff is excluded.

examples.description: Surface missing or inconsistent inventory timestamps.
examples.example_sql: SELECT COUNTIF(created_at IS NULL) AS missing_created, COUNTIF(sold_at < created_at) AS invalid_chronology FROM inventory
examples.illustrative_answer: One authorized record lacks a creation timestamp and another records sale before creation. Neither can establish valid available stock; investigate the underlying records.
method_notes: Query inventory rather than prefiltered stock for quality checks.

examples.description: Estimate coverage only with compatible sales evidence.
examples.illustrative_answer: A coverage estimate requires a scoped sales artifact with sold units, a complete observation interval and matching product IDs. With those inputs, divide modeled unsold units by units per calendar day; zero observed demand gives undefined coverage.
method_notes: Require authorized demand data, never use example numbers as demand.
Label continued-demand assumptions and exclude replenishment claims.

examples.description: Separate recorded stock analysis from procurement decisions.
examples.illustrative_answer: The available inventory records can support a stock review, but they do not establish an order quantity without supplier lead times, reservations, incoming orders and a chosen service-level policy. No purchase order has been placed.
method_notes: All transfer/procurement outcomes are proposals, not executed actions.
